subject: Telemetry-driven rightsize proposal for Dedicated GPU pool + pricing
messages:
From: Mike Jacobs <mike@stratagem.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — sizing and pricing question

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the chat earlier. We're evaluating a Dedicated pool for our inference layer and want a telemetry-backed recommendation before we talk commit / discounts. Quick snapshot of current production traffic (Aug–Sep):
- Peak request rate: 30 requests/sec (sustained 3–4 minute peaks)
- Baseline burstable: 8–12 requests/sec
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + completion): ~920 tokens (prompt ~800, completion ~120)
- Typical context: 8k tokens for few-shot prompts; we sometimes use 16k for scheduled runs
- Observed peak concurrent streams: ~110 (streaming responses)
- Target p95 latency: <= 300 ms for the 13B model tier; we can allow up to 600 ms for 70B fallbacks
- Model mix today: ~75% Llama-13B family, 25% Llama-70B family (we may add quantized variants)

I've attached a CSV export from our telemetry (stratagem_telemetry_aug-sep.csv). Can you recommend:
1) A baseline GPU pool size (GPU type & count) that meets the p95 target for sustained traffic
2) How much burst capacity / credits to include (we expect occasional 2x spikes)
3) A 12- and 24-month reserved commit recommendation and an initial price ballpark / discount range

Procurement will want a single-line summary they can present to finance. Appreciate any quick math you can share.

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Jacobs
Head of Platform
Stratagem.ai

Team — forwarding Stratagem's telemetry. They want a telemetry-backed rightsize + pricing. Key asks are baseline GPUs, burst sizing, and commit/discount guidance.

Notes / quick thoughts:
- Peak tokens/sec estimate: 30 rps * 920 tokens = 27,600 tokens/sec sustained peaks (they claim 30 sustained for a few minutes).
- Concurrent streams ~110 means we need to account for concurrency and per-stream latency (prefetch/KV cache impact for long context).
- Model mix favors 13B; design pool for 13B p95 <=300ms and gracefully degrade 70B to slower nodes; consider int8 quantized 70B as fallback to reduce cost.

Marissa — can you run a throughput calc (tokens/sec per GPU) for our H100-equivalent and A100-equivalent profiles with the 13B/70B mix and 8k context? Please include fallback paths (quantized 70B).
Ben — I'll need recommended commit tiers and a discount framework (12m vs 24m), plus suggested burst credits and a pricing anchor. Laura — any SLA or operational constraints we should call out to the customer up-front (maintenance windows, guaranteed burst vs best-effort)?

I'll assemble a short proposal for Mike once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com

Date: 2026-09-23T08:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — sizing and pricing question

Markus — ran the telemetry through our rightsize calc and here's the summary (assumptions noted below). Full calc attached (pool_rightsize_calc.xlsx).

Assumptions / model perf approximations (8k context):
- H100-80GB equivalent throughput (13B, optimized runtime, int8 not used): ~9,000 tokens/sec per GPU at p95 <= 300ms for single-stream priority workloads.
- H100 throughput (70B, float16): ~3,500 tokens/sec per GPU at p95 ~500–700ms (70B heavier). Quantized 70B (int8): ~7,000 tokens/sec with higher variance.
- We assume 75% of requests hit 13B path, 25% route to 70B or quantized fallback.

Workload math (peak):
- Total tokens/sec = 30 rps * 920 = 27,600 tps
- 13B share tokens/sec = 0.75 * 27,600 = 20,700 tps
- 70B share tokens/sec = 0.25 * 27,600 = 6,900 tps

Baseline recommendation (target p95 <= 300ms for majority):
- Option A (conservative, no quantization): 13B on H100s -> 20,700 / 9,000 ≈ 2.3 -> 3 GPUs for 13B traffic; 70B -> 6,900 / 3,500 ≈ 2.0 -> 2 GPUs. Total: 5 GPUs (H100-equivalent).
- Option B (cost-optimized, quantized 70B fallback): 13B -> 3 GPUs; quantized 70B -> 1 GPU (7,000 tps). Total: 4 GPUs.

Burst handling / concurrency:
- Because they have ~110 concurrent streams, we recommend reserving headroom equal to 30% over baseline to keep tail latency acceptable during bursts. That brings Option B to ~5 GPUs effective capacity for sustained 2x short spikes.
- Alternatively, offer a burst credit pool that allows an additional 2 GPUs-worth of burst for up to 15 minutes per day (configurable).

Operational notes:
- For 8k context, KV cache increases memory pressure — H100-80GB recommended.
- If they plan heavy 16k context runs, add one extra GPU or schedule those runs on separate capacity.

I'm attaching the detailed calc and a short slide with the tradeoffs.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: 2026-09-24T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — sizing and pricing question

Markus / Marissa — pricing frame and commit options below. Numbers are illustrative — fine tune once legal/procurement asks for SOW.

Pricing anchors (H100-equivalent unit):
- On-demand rate (hosted/Dedicated burst) equivalent: $120k / GPU / year (list internal number for modeling).
- 12-month reserved commit (per GPU): 18% discount off on-demand -> ~$98.4k / GPU / year effective
- 24-month reserved commit: 24% discount -> ~$91.2k / GPU / year effective

Package proposals to present: 
- Conservative Package (Option A from Marissa): 5 GPUs reserved (H100-eq) 
  - 12m commit: 5 * $98.4k = $492k/year
  - Suggested commercial: 18% standard discount + $20k onboarding credit + 10% cloud marketplace fee concessions if needed
  - Burst: include 2 GPU-equivalent burst credits (15 min/day) as part of SLA

- Cost-optimized Package (Option B): 4 GPUs reserved + 1 GPU burst pool (elastic)
  - 12m commit: 4 * $98.4k = $393.6k/year
  - Suggested commercial: 20% discount if they sign 24m (move to $314k/year effective); include one-time migration credit $15k

Negotiation playbook:
- If they push on price, move them to 24m for an additional 6% discount and commit to fixed unit price for the term.
- Offer a limited-time pilot (30 days at 1 GPU + 50% off second GPU) to validate perf; pilot fees apply to commit if they convert within 60 days.

Laura — SLA wording: we usually guarantee uptime and a baseline throughput (tokens/sec) per reserved GPU; burst credits are best-effort beyond guaranteed capacity. If Stratagem requires firm burst guarantees we need to map that into their commit level (i.e., pay for extra reserved units).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: markus.klein@redwood.com

Date: 2026-09-29T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: telemetry-backed rightsize + reserved commit options (summary)

Hi Mike — thanks for the telemetry. Putting our recommendations in one place so procurement/finance can review. See attached short proposal (dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf) and the sizing workbook (pool_rightsize_calc.xlsx).

Executive summary (recommended starting offering):
- Recommended baseline pool: 4 H100-equivalent GPUs (cost-optimized path with quantized 70B fallback).
- Effective provisioning: 4 reserved GPUs for normal operations + 1 GPU worth of burst credits to cover 15-min daily spikes (or equivalent elastic burst). We calculate this meets your p95 <= 300ms target for the 13B path and provides graceful fallback for 70B traffic.
- Tokens/sec capacity (sustained): ~25k tps guaranteed; burst to ~40k tps for short intervals with the burst pool. This aligns with your reported peak of ~27.6k tps but gives 10–15% headroom for variance and concurrency.

Commercial options (high level):
- 12-month commit (recommended trial): 4 GPUs reserved at ~18% discount off on-demand -> annualized anchor ~$394k. Includes: 2 weeks onboarding support, 1-month performance validation, 1-time migration credit $15k, and burst credits as noted.
- 24-month commit: move to ~24% discount -> annualized anchor ~$314k/year (lower effective unit). Additional concessions: extended support SLAs and one full quarter of free burst credits for the first 3 months of the term.

Operational points:
- If Stratagem expects frequent 16k-context runs, add one additional GPU to the pool or schedule those runs outside peak windows.
- Maintenance windows are transparent and we provide a runbook for failovers; burst credits are best-effort by default unless priced into a higher commit tier.

Next steps (quick wins):
1) If this looks reasonable, procurement can request a formal Quote + SOW (we'll attach DocuSign link).
2) We can schedule a 60-minute run-through with engineering to validate the attached workload calc and confirm any model-mix changes.
3) If you want stronger burst guarantees, let us know expected burst frequency and duration so we can price accordingly.

Attachments: dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf (summary + pricing), pool_rightsize_calc.xlsx (detailed math), stratagem_telemetry_aug-sep.csv (your telemetry).

Happy to hop on a call to walk through.

Best,
